svg.aria-label: How to write இ: one unbroken stroke · 7 movements
svg.title: Writing இ
svg.desc: 7 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of இ (tamil), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansTamil-Static.ttf. Stroke order after Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 4, இ (Univ. of Texas at Austin), p. 192 <https://sites.la.utexas.edu/tamilscript/files/2009/08/hw_lettersinstructions.pdf>. Source note on variation: Tamil handwriting is taught with school-to-school variation; there is no single national stroke-order standard. Appendix I Frame 4 numbers seven hand-movements for இ. Native writers draw them as one continuous stroke, and this ductus follows the seven movements in order without lifting. The bundled Noto Sans Tamil outline is one unbroken line: the inner right curve runs straight on down one lower diagonal into the lower-left loop, and the lower-right loop runs on up the other diagonal into the outer left side, so movement 3 goes down the first diagonal, movement 6 climbs the second, and no movement retraces ink. In HP Labs India's online Tamil handwriting data (the LipiTk 4.0 Tamil isolated-character recognizer, trained on hpl-tamil-iso-char), 100% of the 30 stored prototypes of இ are a single pen-down stroke.
svg.text: How it is written — one unbroken stroke · 7 movements
Stroke order after Sankaran Radhakrishnan, Tamil Script Learners Manual, Appendix I: Hand-movements, Frame 4, இ (Univ. of Texas at Austin), p. 192
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
